cases.name: the area is calculated, not typed in

exercise1.hint: Store the two numbers in variables first, then print(length * width) so the calculation is the code rather than the answer.

cases.name: uses parentheses to force the addition first

exercise2.hint: Without parentheses Python multiplies before it adds, so 10 + 5 * 3 - 8 gives 17. The parentheses are what make the addition happen first.

questions.explain: A single slash always gives a float, even when the numbers divide evenly.
Double slash is floor division: it divides and discards the remainder.
The modulo operator gives the remainder. It is how you test whether a number divides evenly.
Multiplication binds tighter than addition, so this is 2 + 12. Parentheses are how you override that.

questions.prompt: How do you make the addition happen first?
questions.explain: Parentheses are evaluated first, which is the P in PEMDAS.
